html:
A Soviet silent film made in 1925 by Sergei Eisenstein, which tells the story of a mutiny on a Russian battleship in 1905. It is one of the most influential films ever made.

The real mutiny broke out on the Black Sea fleet during the revolution of 1905, when sailors rose over rotten meat and their officers' brutality. In the film the sailors take the ship, and the people of Odessa gather to support them. Then troops march down a great flight of steps, shooting into the crowd. A pram bounces down the steps. The massacre on the steps did not happen as shown, but the scene became famous.

Eisenstein built the film on montage: short shots cut together for shock and rhythm, so that the meaning comes from the clash between images. His ideas changed film editing around the world and are still taught. The film was made for the twentieth anniversary of 1905 as revolutionary propaganda, and it was banned for years in several countries.
